Survey the Pathland repo's web/SSR path in depth (be very thorough) and produce a precise inventory plus a gap list. This is READ-ONLY research; do not modify anything.

Repo root: /Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland

Context: Pathland is a binary opcode UI protocol (16-byte opcodes) with an SSR HTML renderer + a vanilla-JS hydration client (app.js) used by Spring Boot and Quarkus demos. The user wants to turn it into a credible replacement for HTMX for enterprise SRE teams (server-driven UI, minimal client JS, WebSocket deltas). I need to know exactly what exists today to build a gap list.

Please inventory and report:

1. **The web client (app.js)**: Find every copy of app.js under lib/java/*/src/main/resources/**. For the main/reference copy, report: what it does (hydration by data-pathland-id, PLPL batch decode, delta application), how it sends raw-input events over the WebSocket, whether it has any reconnection logic / heartbeat / backoff / session-resync, how it handles server disconnect, error handling, and whether it is a self-contained versioned artifact or a demo helper. Quote key function names.

2. **SSR HTML renderers**: 
   - Java: lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/com/pathland/render/html/... — list EVERY view component that has an HTML element mapping and the exact element/tag + attributes it emits (e.g. Text->span, Button->button, TextField->input[type=text]?, Toggle->checkbox?, Slider->input[type=range]?, Picker->select?, Spacer->div). Note which components from spec/PRIMITIVES.md have NO mapping yet. Report whether it emits: form semantics (input name=, label for=, form=), ARIA attributes, role attributes.
   - Rust: lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs — same question, which components map to what HTML elements, and whether the Rust one is used by any runnable demo today.

3. **Demos (transport + sessions)**: In lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo and pathland-quarkus-demo: how the WebSocket is set up (path, session handling), how per-session State/PersistentState works, how frames/events are batched (transport batching policy), and whether there is ANY observability/metrics/logging beyond plain logging. Any CSRF / origin / auth checks on the WS? Any heartbeat or reconnect support?

4. **Existing tests**: What test coverage exists for the HTML renderers (golden/round-trip), the app.js client (is there ANY JS test?), and the transport.

5. **Repo conventions**: Where would a reusable JS client and docs naturally live (is there a docs/ dir, a lib/js or similar, a top-level README structure)? List existing docs/*.md files.

Return a structured report with file paths + line numbers for the key items, a component-by-HTML-element mapping table, and a clear "gaps" list organized by: transport resilience, accessibility, form semantics, observability, security, and client artifact/versioning. Do not propose fixes — just inventory what exists and what does not.
I'll survey the repo thoroughly. Let me start with broad structural exploration.

31: // Read a length-prefixed string (`[u32 len][bytes]`) at a relative offset.
32: function readString(strings, offset) {
33:     const view = new DataView(strings.buffer, strings.byteOffset, strings.byteLength);
34:     const len = view.getUint32(offset, true);
35:     const bytes = strings.subarray(offset + 4, offset + 4 + len);
36:     return new TextDecoder().decode(bytes);

39: function applyBatch(bytes) {
40:     const view = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength);
41:     const opcodeCount = view.getUint32(12, true);
42:     const opcodesEnd = 16 + opcodeCount * 16;
43:     const stringsLen = view.getUint32(opcodesEnd, true);
44:     const stringsStart = opcodesEnd + 4;
45:     const strings = bytes.subarray(stringsStart, stringsStart + stringsLen);
46: 
47:     for (let i = 0; i < opcodeCount; i++) {
48:         const pos = 16 + i * 16;
49:         const category = view.getUint8(pos);
50:         const command = view.getUint8(pos + 1);
51:         const a = view.getUint32(pos + 4, true);
52:         const b = view.getUint32(pos + 8, true);
53:         const c = view.getUint32(pos + 12, true);
54:         if (category === CAT_STYLE && command === CMD_SET_TEXT) {
55:             const el = byId.get(a);
56:             if (!el) continue;
57:             const text = readString(strings, b);
58:             // Text fields/editors carry their value in the input; other controls
59:             // carry their label in an inner span (textContent would clobber it).
60:             const input = el.querySelector("input[type=text]");
61:             if (input) input.value = text;
62:             else {
63:                 const textarea = el.querySelector("textarea");
64:                 if (textarea) textarea.value = text;
65:                 else {
66:                     const span = el.querySelector(".pathland-text");
67:                     if (span) span.textContent = text;
68:                     else el.textContent = text;
69:                 }
70:             }
71:         } else if (category === CAT_STYLE && command === CMD_SET_DATE) {
72:             const el = byId.get(a);
73:             if (!el) continue;
74:             const date = el.matches("input[type=date]") ? el : el.querySelector("input[type=date]");
75:             if (date) {

81:             const propId = b & 0xffff;

83:             if (valueType === VAL_STRING) {
84:                 const el = byId.get(a);

92:                     if (input) input.placeholder = text;
93:                 }
94:             } else if (propId === PROP_SELECTED) {
95:                 const el = byId.get(a);
96:                 if (!el) continue;

98:                 if (input) input.checked = (c & 0xff) !== 0;

100:                 const el = byId.get(a);
101:                 if (!el) continue;
102:                 const range = el.querySelector("input[type=range]");
103:                 if (range) range.value = String(f32FromBits(c));
104:                 const stepText = el.querySelector(".pathland-stepper span");
105:                 if (stepText) stepText.textContent = String(Math.round(f32FromBits(c) * 100) / 100);

107:                 const el = byId.get(a);
108:                 if (!el) continue;
109:                 const select = el.matches("select") ? el : el.querySelector("select");
110:                 if (select) select.value = String(c);

112:                 const el = byId.get(a);
113:                 if (!el) continue;

107:     /// Constraint/style CSS decoded from the node's properties (padding, color,
108:     /// fonts, opacity, visibility, size, text alignment/truncation). Empty when
109:     /// the node has no such properties.
110:     fn style_css(&self) -> String {
111:         let mut css = String::new();
112: 
113:         // Layout modifiers.
114:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::PADDING) {
115:             let v = f32::from_bits(*bits);
116:             if v != 0.0 {
117:                 css.push_str(&format!("padding:{v}px;"));
118:             }
119:         }
120:         for (prop, side) in [
121:             (property_id::PADDING_TOP, "top"),
122:             (property_id::PADDING_RIGHT, "right"),
123:             (property_id::PADDING_BOTTOM, "bottom"),
124:             (property_id::PADDING_LEFT, "left"),
125:         ] {
126:             if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&prop) {
127:                 let v = f32::from_bits(*bits);
128:                 if v != 0.0 {
129:                     css.push_str(&format!("padding-{side}:{v}px;"));
130:                 }
131:             }
132:         }
133:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::WIDTH) {
134:             css.push_str(&format!("width:{};", size_css(f32::from_bits(*bits))));
135:         }
136:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::HEIGHT) {
137:             css.push_str(&format!("height:{};", size_css(f32::from_bits(*bits))));
138:         }
139: 
140:         // Appearance.
141:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::COLOR) {
142:             css.push_str(&format!("color:{};", rgba(*bits)));
143:         }
144:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR) {
145:             css.push_str(&format!("background-color:{};", rgba(*bits)));
146:         }
147:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::FONT_SIZE) {
148:             let v = f32::from_bits(*bits);
149:             if v > 0.0 {
150:                 css.push_str(&format!("font-size:{v}px;"));
151:             }
152:         }
153:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::FONT_WEIGHT) {
154:             let v = f32::from_bits(*bits);
155:             if v > 0.0 {
156:                 css.push_str(&format!("font-weight:{v};"));
157:             }
158:         }
159:         if let Some(family) = self.strings.get(&property_id::FONT_FAMILY) {
160:             css.push_str(&format!("font-family:'{}';", family.replace('\'', "\\'")));
161:         }
162:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::OPACITY) {
163:             let v = f32::from_bits(*bits);
164:             if v < 1.0 {
165:                 css.push_str(&format!("opacity:{v};"));
166:             }
167:         }
168:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::VISIBLE) {
169:             if *bits == 0 {
170:                 css.push_str("display:none;");
171:             }
172:         }
173:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::Z_INDEX) {
174:             css.push_str(&format!("z-index:{};", f32::from_bits(*bits) as i32));
175:         }
176: 
177:         // Text layout.
178:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::LINE_LIMIT) {
179:             let n = *bits;
180:             if n != 0 {
181:                 css.push_str(&format!(
182:                     "display:-webkit-box;-webkit-line-clamp:{n};-webkit-box-orient:vertical;overflow:hidden;"
183:                 ));
184:             }
185:         }
186:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::TEXT_ALIGNMENT) {
187:             let idx = (f32::from_bits(*bits) as u8).min(2) as usize;
188:             css.push_str(&format!("text-align:{};", ["left", "center", "right"][idx]));
189:         }
190:         if self.properties.contains_key(&property_id::TRUNCATION_MODE) {
191:             css.push_str("text-overflow:ellipsis;overflow:hidden;");
192:         }
193: 
194:         css
195:     }

197:     /// Border CSS, decoded from `BORDER_WIDTH`/`BORDER_COLOR`/`BORDER_RADIUS`/
198:     /// `BORDER_EDGES` (empty when the node has no border).
199:     fn border_style(&self) -> String {
200:         let Some(width_bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::BORDER_WIDTH) else {
201:             return String::new();
202:         };
203:         let width = f32::from_bits(*width_bits);
204:         let color = self
205:             .properties
206:             .get(&property_id::BORDER_COLOR)
207:             .copied()
208:             .unwrap_or(0xFF00_0000);
209:         let edges = self
210:             .properties
211:             .get(&property_id::BORDER_EDGES)
212:             .copied()
213:             .unwrap_or(border_edges::ALL);
214: 
215:         let (r, g, b, a) = unpack_color(color);
216:         let mut css = String::new();
217:         for (flag, side) in [
218:             (border_edges::TOP, "top"),
219:             (border_edges::LEADING, "left"),
220:             (border_edges::BOTTOM, "bottom"),
221:             (border_edges::TRAILING, "right"),
222:         ] {
223:             if edges & flag != 0 {
224:                 css.push_str(&format!("border-{side}:{width}px solid rgba({r},{g},{b},{a});"));
225:             }
226:         }
227:         if let Some(radius) = self.properties.get(&property_id::BORDER_RADIUS) {
228:             let radius = f32::from_bits(*radius);
229:             if radius != 0.0 {
230:                 css.push_str(&format!("border-radius:{radius}px;"));
231:             }
232:         }
233:         css
234:     }
235: }

237: /// Unpack a `0xAARRGGBB` color into `(r, g, b, alpha)` where `alpha` is `0..1`.
238: fn unpack_color(argb: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32, f32) {
239:     let r = (argb >> 16) & 0xFF;
240:     let g = (argb >> 8) & 0xFF;
241:     let b = argb & 0xFF;
242:     let a = ((argb >> 24) & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0;
243:     (r, g, b, a)
244: }

246: /// A `0xAARRGGBB` color as a CSS `rgba(r,g,b,a)` string.
247: fn rgba(argb: u32) -> String {
248:     let (r, g, b, a) = unpack_color(argb);
249:     format!("rgba({r},{g},{b},{a})")
250: }

275: /// Convert days since the Unix epoch (negative = before 1970) to a Gregorian
276: /// `(year, month, day)` using the civil-from-days algorithm.
277: fn days_to_date(days: i32) -> (i32, u32, u32) {
278:     let z = i64::from(days) + 719_468;
279:     let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;
280:     let doe = z - era * 146_097;
281:     let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
282:     let y = yoe + era * 400;
283:     let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
284:     let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
285:     let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
286:     let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
287:     let y = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
288:     (y as i32, m as u32, d as u32)
289: }

291: /// Millis of day → `(hours, minutes, seconds)`.
292: fn millis_to_hms(millis: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32) {
293:     let total = millis / 1000;
294:     (total / 3600, (total % 3600) / 60, total % 60)
295: }

353: /// Applies opcode frames to a retained node map and renders it as HTML.
354: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
355: pub struct HtmlRenderer {
356:     nodes: BTreeMap<u32, Node>,
357: }

359: impl HtmlRenderer {
360:     /// Create an empty renderer.
361:     #[must_use]
362:     pub fn new() -> Self {
363:         Self::default()
364:     }
365: 
366:     /// Apply a transport `Frame` (a self-contained opcode frame + string
367:     /// section), mutating the retained description. The frame may come from
368:     /// [`frame_from_slices`] (in-process), a network decoder, or a ring.
369:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame) {
370:         for op in frame.opcodes() {
371:             match op.category() {
372:                 category::TREE => self.apply_tree(op.command(), op),
373:                 category::STYLE => self.apply_style(op.command(), op, frame),
374:                 _ => {}
375:             }
376:         }
377:     }
378: 
379:     /// Apply a frame from raw opcodes + a string section, building an in-memory
380:     /// [`Frame`] (via the in-process transport seam) and delegating to
381:     /// [`Self::apply_frame`].
382:     pub fn apply(&mut self, opcodes: &[Opcode], strings: &[u8]) {
383:         let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE);
384:         let frame = frame_from_slices(&mut slots, strings, opcodes);
385:         self.apply_frame(&frame);
386:     }

388:     fn apply_tree(&mut self, command: u8, op: Opcode) {
389:         match command {
390:             tree::CREATE_NODE => {
391:                 let id = op.a();
392:                 let component = op.b() as u16;
393:                 self.nodes.insert(id, Node::new(component));
394:             }
395:             tree::DELETE_NODE => {
396:                 self.nodes.remove(&op.a());
397:             }
398:             tree::INSERT_CHILD => {
399:                 let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
400:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
401:                     node.children.push(child);
402:                 }
403:             }
404:             tree::REMOVE_CHILD => {
405:                 let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
406:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
407:                     node.children.retain(|&c| c != child);
408:                 }
409:             }
410:             tree::MOVE_CHILD => {
411:                 let (parent, child, index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c());
412:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
413:                     node.children.retain(|&c| c != child);
414:                     let index = (index as usize).min(node.children.len());
415:                     node.children.insert(index, child);
416:                 }
417:             }
418:             _ => {}
419:         }
420:     }
421: 
422:     fn apply_style(&mut self, command: u8, op: Opcode, frame: &Frame) {
423:         match command {
424:             style::SET_TEXT => {
425:                 if let Some(text) = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok() {
426:                     if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
427:                         node.text = Some(text.to_string());
428:                     }
429:                 }
430:             }
431:             style::SET_PROPERTY => {
432:                 let property = (op.b() & 0xFFFF) as u16;
433:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
434:                     let vt = (op.b() >> 16) as u8;
435:                     if vt == value_type::STRING {
436:                         if let Some(text) = frame.arena_str(op.c()).ok() {
437:                             node.strings.insert(property, text.to_string());
438:                         }
439:                     } else {
440:                         node.properties.insert(property, op.c());
441:                     }
442:                 }
443:             }
444:             style::SET_DATE => {
445:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
446:                     // B = days since epoch (I32), C = millis of day (U32).
447:                     node.date = Some((op.b() as i32, op.c()));
448:                 }
449:             }
450:             _ => {}
451:         }
452:     }

490:     fn render_node(&self, id: u32) -> String {
491:         let Some(node) = self.nodes.get(&id) else {
492:             return String::new();
493:         };
494:         let children: String = node
495:             .children
496:             .iter()
497:             .map(|&child| self.render_node(child))
498:             .collect();
499:         let data_id = format!(" data-pathland-id=\"{id}\"");
500:         let css = format!("{}{}", node.style_css(), node.border_style());
501:         let style = style_attr(&css);
502:         let event = event_attrs(node);
503:         let aria = aria_attrs(node);
504: 
505:         match node.component {
506:             component_type::VSTACK => self.wrap_stack(id, "column", node, &children, &css, &event, &aria),
507:             component_type::HSTACK => self.wrap_stack(id, "row", node, &children, &css, &event, &aria),
508:             component_type::LAZY_VSTACK => {
509:                 self.wrap_stack(id, "column", node, &children, &css, &event, &aria)
510:             }
511:             component_type::LAZY_HSTACK => {
512:                 self.wrap_stack(id, "row", node, &children, &css, &event, &aria)
513:             }
514:             component_type::TEXT => {
515:                 let text = escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default());
516:                 format!("<span{data_id}{event}{aria}{style}>{text}</span>")
517:             }
518:             component_type::BUTTON => {
519:                 // Composite Override Mode: children present → custom body.
520:                 let body = if node.children.is_empty() {
521:                     escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default())
522:                 } else {
523:                     children
524:                 };
525:                 format!("<button{data_id}{event}{aria}{style}>{body}</button>")
526:             }
527:             component_type::TOGGLE => {
528:                 let toggle_style = node.f32_property(property_id::TOGGLE_STYLE, 0.0).round() as u8;
529:                 let checked = if node.checked() { " checked" } else { "" };
530:                 let body = if node.children.is_empty() {
531:                     format!(
532:                         "<span class=\"pathland-text\">{}</span>",
533:                         escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default())
534:                     )
535:                 } else {
536:                     format!("<div class=\"pathland-custom-body\">{children}</div>")
537:                 };
538:                 match toggle_style {
539:                     1 => format!(
540:                         "<label{data_id}{event}{aria} class=\"pathland-toggle\"{style}><input type=\"checkbox\"{checked}>{body}</label>"
541:                     ),
542:                     2 => {
543:                         let pressed = if node.checked() { "true" } else { "false" };
544:                         format!(
545:                             "<button{data_id}{event}{aria} type=\"button\" aria-pressed=\"{pressed}\"{style}>{body}</button>"
546:                         )
547:                     }
548:                     _ => format!(
549:                         "<label{data_id}{event}{aria} class=\"pathland-toggle\"{style}><input type=\"checkbox\" role=\"switch\"{checked}>{body}</label>"
550:                     ),
551:                 }
552:             }
553:             component_type::SPACER => {
554:                 let css = format!("flex:1;{css}");
555:                 format!("<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"{css}\"></div>")
556:             }
557:             component_type::SLIDER => {
558:                 let min = node.f32_property(property_id::MIN_VALUE, 0.0);
559:                 let max = node.f32_property(property_id::MAX_VALUE, 1.0);
560:                 let value = node.f32_property(property_id::VALUE, min);
561:                 let body = if node.children.is_empty() {
562:                     format!(
563:                         "<span class=\"pathland-text\">{}</span>",
564:                         escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default())
565:                     )
566:                 } else {
567:                     format!("<div class=\"pathland-custom-body\">{children}</div>")
568:                 };
569:                 format!(
570:                     "<label{data_id}{event}{aria} class=\"pathland-slider\"{style}><input type=\"range\" min=\"{min}\" max=\"{max}\" step=\"any\" value=\"{value}\">{body}</label>"
571:                 )
572:             }
573:             component_type::TEXT_FIELD => {
574:                 let value = escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default());
575:                 let label = escape(
576:                     node.strings
577:                         .get(&property_id::LABEL)
578:                         .map(String::as_str)
579:                         .unwrap_or_default(),
580:                 );
581:                 let prompt = escape(
582:                     node.strings
583:                         .get(&property_id::PROMPT)
584:                         .map(String::as_str)
585:                         .unwrap_or_default(),
586:                 );

624:                     "width:{};height:{};background-color:{};{css}",

626:                     size_css(h),
627:                     rgba(fill)
628:                 );
629:                 let shape_css = match kind {
630:                     0 | 4 => "border-radius:50%;",
631:                     2 => {
632:                         let r = node.f32_property(property_id::BORDER_RADIUS, 8.0);
633:                         return format!("<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"{base}border-radius:{r}px;\"></div>");

639:                             rgba(fill)
640:                         );

643:                 };

646:             component_type::DIVIDER => {
647:                 let width = node.f32_property(property_id::BORDER_WIDTH, 1.0);
648:                 let color = node
649:                     .properties
650:                     .get(&property_id::COLOR)
651:                     .copied()
652:                     .map(rgba)
653:                     .unwrap_or_else(|| "rgba(0,0,0,0.2)".to_string());
654:                 format!(
655:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"height:0;border-top:{width}px solid {color};\"></div>"
656:                 )
657:             }
658:             component_type::PROGRESS_VIEW => {
659:                 let indeterminate = node.f32_property(property_id::IS_INDETERMINATE, 0.0) != 0.0
660:                     || node.f32_property(property_id::PROGRESS, -1.0) < 0.0;
661:                 if indeterminate {
662:                     format!("<div{data_id} class=\"pathland-spinner\"{style}></div>")

665:                     let max = node.f32_property(property_id::MAX_VALUE, 1.0);
666:                     format!(
667:                         "<progress{data_id}{event}{aria} value=\"{value}\" max=\"{max}\"{style}></progress>"
668:                     )
669:                 }
670:             }
671:             component_type::GAUGE => {
672:                 let min = node.f32_property(property_id::MIN_VALUE, 0.0);
673:                 let max = node.f32_property(property_id::MAX_VALUE, 1.0);
674:                 let value = node.f32_property(property_id::VALUE, min);
675:                 let pct = if max > min {
676:                     ((value - min) / (max - min)).clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 100.0
677:                 } else {
678:                     0.0
679:                 };

682:                 )

685:                 let cols = grid_columns(node);
686:                 let gap = node
687:                     .spacing()
688:                     .map(|s| format!("gap:{s}px;"))
689:                     .unwrap_or_default();
690:                 let template = cols
691:                     .map(|n| format!("grid-template-columns:repeat({n},1fr);"))
692:                     .unwrap_or_default();
693:                 let flow = if node.component == component_type::LAZY_HGRID {
694:                     "grid-auto-flow:column;grid-auto-columns:1fr;"
695:                 } else {
696:                     ""
697:                 };
698:                 format!(
699:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"display:grid;{template}{flow}{gap}{css}\">{children}</div>"
700:                 )
701:             }
702:             component_type::SCROLLVIEW => {
703:                 format!("<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"overflow:auto;{css}\">{children}</div>")
704:             }
705:             component_type::ZSTACK => {
706:                 let inner: String = node
707:                     .children
708:                     .iter()
709:                     .map(|&child| {
710:                         let child_html = self.render_node(child);
711:                         if child_html.is_empty() {
712:                             String::new()
713:                         } else {
714:                             format!("<div style=\"position:absolute;inset:0\">{child_html}</div>")
715:                         }
716:                     })
717:                     .collect();
718:                 format!(
719:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"position:relative;width:100%;height:100%;{css}\">{inner}</div>"
720:                 )
721:             }
722:             component_type::STEPPER => {
723:                 let min = node.f32_property(property_id::MIN_VALUE, 0.0);
724:                 let max = node.f32_property(property_id::MAX_VALUE, 100.0);
725:                 let value = node.f32_property(property_id::VALUE, min);
726:                 let step = node.f32_property(property_id::STEP_VALUE, 1.0);
727:                 format!(
728:                     "<input{data_id}{event}{aria} type=\"number\" min=\"{min}\" max=\"{max}\" step=\"{step}\" value=\"{value}\"{style}>"
729:                 )
730:             }
731:             component_type::DATE_PICKER => {
732:                 let mode = node.f32_property(property_id::DATE_PICKER_MODE, 0.0).round() as u8;
733:                 let (t, value) = match node.date {
734:                     Some((days, millis)) => match mode {
735:                         1 => {
736:                             let (hh, mm, _) = millis_to_hms(millis);
737:                             ("time", format!("{hh:02}:{mm:02}"))
738:                         }
739:                         2 => {
740:                             let (y, m, d) = days_to_date(days);
741:                             let (hh, mm, _) = millis_to_hms(millis);
742:                             (
743:                                 "datetime-local",
744:                                 format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}T{hh:02}:{mm:02}"),
745:                             )
746:                         }
747:                         _ => {
748:                             let (y, m, d) = days_to_date(days);
749:                             ("date", format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}"))
750:                         }
751:                     },
752:                     None => ("date", String::new()),
753:                 };
754:                 format!("<input{data_id}{event}{aria} type=\"{t}\" value=\"{value}\"{style}>")
755:             }
756:             component_type::PICKER => {
757:                 let selected = node.u32_property(property_id::SELECTION, 0);
758:                 let options: String = node
759:                     .children
760:                     .iter()
761:                     .enumerate()
762:                     .map(|(i, &child)| {
763:                         let label = self
764:                             .nodes
765:                             .get(&child)
766:                             .and_then(|n| n.text.clone())
767:                             .unwrap_or_default();
768:                         let sel = if i as u32 == selected { " selected" } else { "" };
769:                         format!("<option value=\"{i}\"{sel}>{}</option>", escape(&label))
770:                     })
771:                     .collect();
772:                 format!("<select{data_id}{event}{aria}{style}>{options}</select>")
773:             }
774:             component_type::MENU => {
775:                 let label = escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default());
776:                 format!(
777:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} role=\"menu\"{style}><button type=\"button\">{label}</button>{children}</div>"
778:                 )
779:             }
780:             component_type::COLOR_PICKER => {
781:                 let color = node.u32_property(property_id::COLOR_VALUE, 0xFF00_0000);
782:                 let hex = format!(
783:                     "#{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}",
784:                     (color >> 16) & 0xFF,
785:                     (color >> 8) & 0xFF,
786:                     color & 0xFF
787:                 );
788:                 format!("<input{data_id}{event}{aria} type=\"color\" value=\"{hex}\"{style}>")
789:             }
790:             component_type::COMMENT => String::new(),
791:             _ => String::new(),
792:         }
793:     }

1: //! Batching policy and buffering for network transport.
2: //!
3: //! `Batcher` accumulates frames against a [`BatchPolicy`] and flushes a single
4: //! serialized batch when either the time interval since the first buffered
5: //! opcode elapses **or** the accumulated byte size reaches the threshold —
6: //! first trigger wins.
7: 
8: use alloc::vec::Vec;
9: use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
10: 
11: use pathland_core::Opcode;
12: 
13: use crate::batch::encode_batch;
14: use crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST;
15: 
16: /// Default time interval before a batch is flushed (4 ms).
17: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(4);
18: /// Default max batch byte size (conservative network frame / MTU).
19: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_BYTES: usize = 1400;
20: 
21: /// Flush thresholds for network batching.
22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
23: pub struct BatchPolicy {
24:     /// Flush when this much time has elapsed since the first buffered opcode.
25:     pub max_interval: Duration,
26:     /// Flush when the accumulated batch reaches this many bytes.
27:     pub max_batch_bytes: usize,
28: }
29: 
30: impl BatchPolicy {
31:     /// Create a policy from a time interval and a max batch size.
32:     pub const fn new(max_interval: Duration, max_batch_bytes: usize) -> Self {
33:         Self {
34:             max_interval,
35:             max_batch_bytes,
36:         }
37:     }
38: 
39:     /// The default policy: 4 ms interval, 1400-byte batches.
40:     pub const fn default_policy() -> Self {
41:         Self::new(DEFAULT_MAX_INTERVAL, DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_BYTES)
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: impl Default for BatchPolicy {

48:     }
49: }

51: /// Accumulates frames into a batch and flushes per [`BatchPolicy`].
52: ///
53: /// The arena is append-only; the batcher ships the bytes appended since the
54: /// last flush (tracked by arena length). If the arena shrank (a `META::RESET`),
55: /// the pending arena is reset so the next flush starts fresh.
56: #[derive(Debug)]
57: pub struct Batcher {
58:     policy: BatchPolicy,
59:     /// Frame count of the first buffered frame.
60:     frame_count: u32,
61:     /// Opcodes buffered since the last flush.
62:     opcodes: Vec<Opcode>,
63:     /// Arena bytes appended since the last flush.
64:     pending_arena: Vec<u8>,
65:     /// Arena length at the last flush.
66:     last_arena_len: usize,
67:     /// When the first opcode of the current batch was buffered.
68:     started: Option<Instant>,
69:     /// Size trigger latched on push.
70:     size_triggered: bool,
71: }
72: 
73: impl Batcher {
74:     /// Create a batcher with the given policy.
75:     pub fn new(policy: BatchPolicy) -> Self {
76:         Self {
77:             policy,
78:             frame_count: 0,
79:             opcodes: Vec::new(),
80:             pending_arena: Vec::new(),
81:             last_arena_len: 0,
82:             started: None,
83:             size_triggered: false,
84:         }
85:     }
86: 
87:     /// Create a batcher with the default policy (4 ms / 1400 B).
88:     pub fn default_policy() -> Self {
89:         Self::new(BatchPolicy::default())
90:     }
91: 
92:     /// Whether no opcodes are currently buffered.
93:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
94:         self.opcodes.is_empty()
95:     }
96: 
97:     /// Number of opcodes buffered since the last flush (diagnostics).
98:     pub fn pending_opcodes(&self) -> usize {
99:         self.opcodes.len()
100:     }
101: 
102:     /// Approximate bytes that would be shipped on flush (diagnostics).
103:     pub fn pending_bytes(&self) -> usize {
104:         self.opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE + self.pending_arena.len() + crate::batch::BATCH_HEADER + 4
105:     }

107:     /// Record a frame (opcodes + the arena's used portion `[0..cursor)`),
108:     /// accumulating the arena delta. Returns `true` if the size trigger fired.
109:     pub fn push_frame(&mut self, frame_count: u32, opcodes: &[Opcode], arena_used: &[u8]) -> bool {
110:         if self.started.is_none() {
111:             self.started = Some(Instant::now());
112:             self.frame_count = frame_count;
113:         }
114:         if arena_used.len() < self.last_arena_len {
115:             // Arena was reset; restart the pending buffer.
116:             self.pending_arena.clear();
117:             self.last_arena_len = 0;
118:         }
119:         self.pending_arena.extend_from_slice(&arena_used[self.last_arena_len..]);
120:         self.last_arena_len = arena_used.len();
121:         self.opcodes.extend_from_slice(opcodes);
122: 
123:         self.size_triggered |= self.pending_bytes() >= self.policy.max_batch_bytes;
124:         self.size_triggered
125:     }

127:     /// Whether the time interval has elapsed since the first buffered opcode.
128:     pub fn interval_elapsed(&self) -> bool {
129:         match self.started {
130:             Some(t) => t.elapsed() >= self.policy.max_interval,
131:             None => false,
132:         }
133:     }

135:     /// Serialize and reset the current buffer, returning the batch bytes.
136:     ///
137:     /// Flushes when `force` is true or either policy trigger fired. Returns
138:     /// `None` when nothing is buffered.
139:     pub fn flush(&mut self, force: bool) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
140:         if self.opcodes.is_empty() {
141:             return None;
142:         }
143:         let should_flush = force || self.size_triggered || self.interval_elapsed();
144:         if !should_flush {
145:             return None;
146:         }
147:         let bytes = encode_batch(
148:             self.frame_count,
149:             GUEST_TO_HOST,
150:             &self.opcodes,
151:             &self.pending_arena,
152:         );
153:         self.opcodes.clear();
154:         self.pending_arena.clear();
155:         self.last_arena_len = 0;
156:         self.started = None;
157:         self.size_triggered = false;
158:         Some(bytes)
159:     }

257: ## Web Client (SSR HTML + app.js)
258: 
259: The browser client is the **SSR HTML renderer** (`pathland-render-html`, and its
260: Java counterpart `com.pathland.render.html`), hydrated by a small vanilla-JS
261: client — `app.js`, shipped in both demos. It hydrates the server-rendered DOM by
262: `data-pathland-id`, decodes each self-contained `PLPL` batch, applies opcode
263: deltas in place, and sends raw-input events back over the `/ws` socket.

265: ## Components & Properties
266: 
267: Component and property IDs are defined in `pathland-core`'s
268: [`constants.rs`](./lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs),
269: documented in [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md), and catalogued by category in
270: [PRIMITIVES.md](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md) (component types), [MODIFIERS.md](./spec/MODIFIERS.md)

272: include `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `VSTACK`, `HSTACK`, `SPACER`, and more; stack
273: constraint properties (`SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, …) drive native layout, styling
274: modifiers (`PADDING`, `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, …) decorate any view, and
275: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` use `-1` = FILL, `-2` = HUG_CONTENT.

278:

282: `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`. See [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system).

1: # pathland-view (Java) — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** August 30, 2026
4: 
5: The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 25+ DSL (`com.pathland.view`):
6: SwiftUI-style views, Angular-style signals, fine-grained emitter, `PLPL` wire
7: codec, lazy FFM ring interop, and cross-platform `State`. Protocol contract:
8: `spec/`.
9: 
10: ## Implemented
11: 
12: - **Construction is `.of()` only**: every concrete view/control exposes a
13:   static `<ViewName>.of(...)` factory (`Text.of`, `VStack.of`,
14:   `Button.of(label, action)`, `Slider.of(binding, min, max)`,
15:   `DatePicker.of(mode, days)`, …); constructors are private and the former
16:   `View.*` static-factory surface is **removed**. `Slider`/`Stepper` are
17:   binding-first (initial value read from the signal); `Toggle` also offers the
18:   SwiftUI-closer `of(label, isOn)` overload; `Color.of(int)` alias.
19: - **One modifier mechanism — no sugar on `View`**: core modifiers are
20:   `ViewModifier` values (`Padding.of(16)`, `ForegroundStyle.of(color)`,
21:   `Border.of(color, width)`, `FrameMod.of(w, h, align)`, …) applied via
22:   `.modifier(...)` (single) or `.modifiers(...)` (several, innermost-first);
23:   the `View` interface has no per-modifier factory methods. Built-in and
24:   application-authored modifiers share the exact same surface (spec `DSL.md`
25:   §5.6); `buttonStyle` is the `ButtonStyleMod` value. Reactive overloads
26:   (`ForegroundStyle.of(Signal)`, `Background.of(Signal)`, `FontSize.of(Signal)`)
27:   re-emit only the bound node. Enum-collision modifier names use the `Mod`
28:   suffix (`FontWeightMod`, `TextAlignmentMod`, `TruncationMod`, `TextCaseMod`,
29:   `FontStyleMod`, `FontDesignMod`, `ControlSizeMod`); `FrameMod` avoids
30:   `emit.Frame`.
31: - **Views**: `View` (open interface), `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Group`
32:   (transparent container, maps to a `VSTACK` node today), `Text`, `Image`,
33:   `Color` (dual identity: a `COLOR` view *and* a value passed into style
34:   modifiers), shapes (`Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Capsule`, `Ellipse`,
35:   `RoundedRectangle`, generic `Shape.of(ShapeKind)` — all `SHAPE` nodes),
36:   `Button`, `TextField`, `Spacer`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
37:   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Divider`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVStack`,
38:   `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker`,
39:   `DatePicker`; `body()` composition; `ButtonStyle`/`ViewModifier`/`Environment`
40:   (ScopedValue).
41: - **Component IDs**: synced to the spec's grouped ranges (`Components.java`:
42:   `TEXT 0x01`, `IMAGE 0x02`, `COLOR 0x03`, `SHAPE 0x04`, `DIVIDER 0x05`,
43:   `SPACER 0x06`, `PROGRESS_VIEW 0x07`, `GAUGE 0x08`, `VSTACK 0x10`,
44:   `HSTACK 0x11`, `ZSTACK 0x12`, `GRID 0x13`, `SCROLLVIEW 0x14`, `LAZY_*`,
45:   `BUTTON 0x20`, `TEXT_FIELD 0x21`, `TEXT_EDITOR 0x22`, `TOGGLE 0x24`,
46:   `SLIDER 0x25`, `STEPPER 0x26`, `DATE_PICKER 0x27`, `PICKER 0x28`,
47:   `MENU 0x29`, `COLOR_PICKER 0x2A`, `COMMENT 0x7F`, …) — frames are spec-valid
48:   and cross-language correct.
49: - **Value controls**: `Toggle`/`Slider`/`Stepper`/`Picker`/`ColorPicker`/
50:   `Menu` bind to writable signals and route `VALUE_CHANGED` through the
51:   emitter's value-input registry; `TextEditor` mirrors `TextField`.
52:   `DatePicker` emits `STYLE::SET_DATE` (and re-emits it on signal change via a
53:   node-level date binding) and routes `DATE_CHANGED` through a dedicated
54:   date-input registry (`RenderResult.dateInputs`).
55: - **Events**: the full catalog round-trips — pointer, `KEY_*`, `VALUE_CHANGED`,
56:   `TEXT_CHANGED`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`,
57:   `WHEEL`, `DATE_CHANGED`; listener bits `0..9` declared
58:   (`Commands.Listeners`). `FrameCodec.decodeEvents` decodes all of them.
59: - **Modifiers** (modifier values applied via `.modifier(...)`/`.modifiers(...)`,
60:   chainable on any view): `Padding`, `ForegroundStyle(Color)` (no `.color()`),
61:   `Background(Color)`, `Tint`, `Opacity`, `FontSize`, `FontWeightMod`, `Border`
62:   (`Border.of(color, width)` canonical + `(color, width, radius)` convenience),
63:   `Visible`/`Hidden`, `FrameMod` (fixed and min/ideal/max), `Offset`, `Position`,
64:   `FixedSize`, `LayoutPriority`, `ZIndex`, `AspectRatio`/`ScaledToFit`/
65:   `ScaledToFill`, `MinimumScaleFactor`, `FontStyleMod`/`Italic`/`FontDesignMod`/
66:   `FontWidth`/`Kerning`/`Tracking`/`BaselineOffset`/`LineSpacing`/`LineLimit`/
67:   `TextAlignmentMod`/`TruncationMod`/`TextCaseMod`/`Underline`/`Strikethrough`/
68:   `FontFamily`, `CornerRadius`, `Shadow`, `Blur`, `Saturation`/`Contrast`/
69:   `Brightness`/`Grayscale`/`HueRotation`/`ColorMultiply`/`ColorInvert`,
70:   `Clipped`/`ClipShape`, `Rotation`, `ScaleEffect`, `Disabled`,
71:   `AllowsHitTesting`, `ControlSizeMod`,
72:   `AccessibilityLabel`/`AccessibilityRole`/`AccessibilityState`, `ImageSource`,
73:   `PointerEvents` (OR-in), `ActionId`/`BindingId`, `TapGesture` (onTapGesture),
74:   `ButtonStyleMod` — `Color` is never a modifier.
75: - **Value types**: `ValueTypes.forProperty` mirrors `value_type_for` —
76:   `COLOR` family → `COLOR`; `VISIBLE`/`ENABLED`/`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`/`UNDERLINE`/
77:   `STRIKETHROUGH`/`COLOR_INVERT`/`ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`/`IS_SECURE`/
78:   `IS_INDETERMINATE`/`FIXED_SIZE_*`/`SELECTED` → `U8`; `LINE_LIMIT`/`SELECTION`/
79:   `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS`/`BORDER_EDGES` → `U32`;
80:   `LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`FONT_FAMILY`/`IMAGE_SOURCE` → `STRING`; enum-valued

1: # Security Policy
2: 
3: Pathland is a network-facing binary protocol: the byte decoders and the C ABI
4: are security-critical surfaces. This policy covers how vulnerabilities are
5: reported and handled.
6: 
7: ## Reporting a vulnerability
8: 
9: **Do not open a public issue for a security vulnerability.** Report it privately
10: to the maintainers:
11: 
12: - Email: `michael@apaq.dk`
13: - Subject prefix: `[Pathland security]`
14: 
15: Please include:
16: 
17: - The affected crate/module and version (or commit).
18: - A description of the vulnerability and its impact.
19: - A minimal reproduction (payload bytes or code) where possible.
20: - Any suggested fix, if you have one.
21: 
22: We aim to acknowledge reports within **5 business days** and to ship a fix (or a
23: mitigation) as soon as a coordinated patch is ready. We will credit reporters in
24: the release notes unless anonymity is requested.
25: 
26: ## Scope
27: 
28: The following are in scope for this policy:
29: 
30: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core` — the `no_std` protocol core (opcode decode,
31:   ring buffer, arena, memory layout).
32: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport` — PLPL batch encode/decode.
33: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-capi` — the `unsafe extern "C"` ring ABI
34:   (`libpathland_core`): pointer-argument handling, zero-copy reads, event drain.
35: - `lib/java/pathland-view` `transport` — `FrameCodec` (PLPL encode/decode).
36: - The demos' vanilla-JS `app.js` web client (PLPL batch decode + hydration in
37:   `lib/java/*-demo/src/main/resources`).
38: 
39: Out of scope: dependencies (report those to their respective projects),
40: development-only tooling, and the demo application code.
41: 
42: ## Security-sensitive guarantees
43: 
44: - Every 16-byte opcode decoder must **reject malformed/truncated input
45:   gracefully** (no panics, no out-of-bounds reads, no hangs) — see the hardening
46:   issues (#37, #38).
47: - The C ABI entry points (`pathland_ring_buffer_push`,
48:   `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, `pathland_core_drain_events`, …) treat
49:   caller-provided pointers as trusted by contract; the bounds guarantees must be
50:   upheld and are audited via Miri/sanitizers in CI.
51: - No secrets or tokens may ever be committed; see
52:   [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md).
53: 
54: ## Security testing
55: 
56: Coverage is tracked by the hardening milestone (issues #37–#39): fuzzing for the
57: Rust/TypeScript/Java decoders, Miri + ASan/UBSan on the C ABI, and bounds fixes.
58: Results will be linked here as they land.
59: 
60: ## Supported versions
61: 
62: The project is pre-1.0 (`wire protocol version 1`). Security fixes land on the
63: default branch and are backported only when a tagged release is actively used;
64: see the [Versioning](README.md#versioning) section.

2: //!
3: //! Producer side serializes Frames into network batches (opcodes + arena delta);
4: //! the consumer decodes them with `BatchDecoder` (see `crate::batch`) back into
5: //! `Frame` views consumed by `RenderTree::apply_frame`. This is the remote/SSR
6: //! path where producer and consumer do **not** share memory.

8: //! The wire format is unchanged from `crate::batch` (magic/version/flags/
9: //! frameCount/opcodeCount/opcodes/arenaDeltaLen/arena).

15: use crate::batch::encode_batch;

17: /// Producer-side network batch encoder.
18: ///
19: /// Buffers opcodes (from Frames) and serializes them into a batch with the
20: /// arena's used-arena slice. Use the `Batcher` helper (`crate::batching`) for a
21: /// time/size flush policy; this type is the bare encoder for explicit flushes.
22: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
23: pub struct NetBatchEncoder {
24:     opcodes: Vec<Opcode>,
25: }
26: 
27: impl NetBatchEncoder {
28:     /// Append a frame's opcodes to the pending batch.
29:     pub fn push_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
30:         self.opcodes.extend(frame.opcodes());
31:     }

33:     /// Append raw opcodes to the pending batch.
34:     pub fn push_opcodes(&mut self, opcodes: &[Opcode]) {
35:         self.opcodes.extend_from_slice(opcodes);
36:     }

39:     /// the buffer. `frame_count` is the covering frame counter.

41:         let bytes = encode_batch(

44:             &self.opcodes,
45:             arena_used,
46:         );
47:         self.opcodes.clear();
48:         bytes
49:     }

53:         self.opcodes.is_empty()
54:     }

8: > **Pathland — an implementable open UI-protocol standard: specification, conformance, validation, hardening, evidence.**
9: 
10: ---
11: 
12: ## 1. Applicant
13:

25: 
26: ## 2. Problem
27: 
28: Server-driven UI (SDUI) and cross-platform UI are fragmented: each platform
29: re-invents retained-mode UI inside a closed framework (Flutter, React Native,
30: Compose Multiplatform, per-vendor SDUI like Airbnb/Lyft/Spotify). The result:
31: 
32: - **No open, language- and platform-agnostic *protocol*** exists for describing
33:   declarative, retained-mode UI — only frameworks that couple the UI model to a
34:   specific runtime.
35: - **No single wire format** serves the full spectrum from embedded (LVGL on
36:   microcontrollers) to in-browser to server-driven enterprise apps, so teams
37:   build and maintain N different UI transports.
38: - **Full-tree serialization is wasteful**: typical SDUI re-sends large JSON
39:   payloads; large, reactive trees cannot sustain high frame rates on the wire or
40:   on the main thread.
41: 
42: ## 3. Innovation — a standard, not another framework
43: 
44: Pathland describes **WHAT** the UI is — structure + constraint properties
45: (VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment) — as a stream of **fixed
46: 16-byte opcodes** in a ring buffer, and never **WHERE** (no layout, no rects).
47: Renderers are **pure functions of the stream**, so the same opcode stream maps
48: onto native widgets on every platform (GTK4, DOM/HTML, LVGL-planned).
49: 
50: The engine is **transport- and process-agnostic**: the producer and consumer
51: only need to exchange bytes, so it runs identically across embedded dual-core,
52: pure in-browser (WASM worker → `SharedArrayBuffer`), native desktop (C ABI /
53: Java FFM over a zero-copy shared ring), and distributed server-driven modes.
54: 
55: **Emission is diff-based and reactive**: a signal bound to a node re-emits only
56: that node's deltas; an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. That is what makes
57: the binary format dramatically smaller than JSON SDUI and fast enough for a
58: 120 FPS interaction target.
59: 
60: The open-standard angle: anyone can implement a Pathland renderer or DSL in any
61: language against the spec and the golden conformance vectors, with no lock-in to
62: a runtime.
63: 
64: ## 4. The specification (exists — split, not monolithic)
65: 
66: The normative spec is **already present** and is the contract this proposal
67: matures:
68: 
69: | File | Content |
70: |------|---------|
71: | `spec/OPCODE.md` | 16-byte opcode format, ring buffer, arena, frame lifecycle, value types, design tokens |
72: | `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` | Primitive views + component IDs |
73: | `spec/MODIFIERS.md` | Core modifiers/properties + value types + enum codes |
74: | `spec/EVENTS.md` | Core events + listener bits |
75: | `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` | Golden byte vectors |
76: | `spec/DSL.md` | Authoring surface (SwiftUI-shaped DSL contract) — informative |
77: 
78: Gap this proposal fills: a **spec index + consolidated property-key registry**
79: and a **cross-language validator** so the split files read as one implementable
80: whole and cannot drift.
81: 
82: ## 5. Scope & work packages (core-first)
83: 
84: The **core is the deliverable** (an implementable open standard); the visual
85: layer is cheap proof, not the product.
86: 
87: | WP | Deliverable | Issue | Effort (h) | Cost @€45/h |
88: |----|-------------|-------|-----------|-------------|
89: | WP1 | `spec/README.md` index + consolidated `0x0000–0xFFFF` property-key registry (derived, cross-checked against all four language surfaces) | #48 | 30 | €1,350 |

93: | WP5 | CI completion (rust + java jobs), **WCAG/ARIA compliance on the SSR HTML renderer**, hosted SSR HTML demo (URL + screenshots), evidence pack | #44, #49, #50 | 45 | €2,025 |
94: | PM / reporting (10%) | NLnet reporting, MoU tracking | — | 15 | €675 |
95: | **Total** | | | **260 h** | **€11,700** |
96: 
97: ## 6. Budget & rates
98: 
99: - **Cost-recovery**, rate **€45/h**, **260 h**, total ask **€11,700**.
100: - NLnet may adjust ineligible costs; the final amount is settled in the MoU.
101: - No other funding sources at present.
102: 
103: ## 7. Evidence layer (the demo is proof, not the product)
104: 
105: The web path already exists (SSR HTML renderer + the demos' vanilla-JS `app.js`
106: client). WP5 makes it visible cheaply: host the existing Quarkus SSR demo at a
107: public URL, include 2 screenshots and the WP4 comparison chart. Reviewers can
108: click a working multi-renderer demo without the core work being a "black box".
109: 
110: ## 8. Prior-art comparison
111: 
112: Airbnb, Lyft and Spotify ship proprietary, per-app SDUI JSON schemas — closed,
113: not an open standard. Flutter, React Native and Compose Multiplatform are
114: frameworks that couple the UI model to one runtime. Native toolkits (GTK,
115: SwiftUI, WinUI) are per-platform and closed. Generic serialization (JSON,
116: Protobuf) is schema-driven data transport, not a UI instruction stream, and
117: re-sends full trees. Pathland is a **16-byte command stream** (tree mutations +
118: properties), open-spec, process/transport-agnostic, with native-element renderers
119: and zero-copy, diff-based emission — an open standard, not another framework.
120: 
121: ## 9. European dimension & ecosystem
122: 
123: - **Digital sovereignty**: an open, Apache-2.0 UI protocol reduces dependence on
124:   US-owned UI stacks — a "made in Europe" alternative for the Open Internet
125:   Stack's *independent and cross-platform development framework* area.
126: - **Open standards / interoperability**: spec + conformance vectors let any EU
127:   vendor implement renderers/DSLs; relevant to W3C/WebUI-type standardization.
128: - **Efficiency/frugality**: 16-byte opcodes + zero-delta emission cut bandwidth
129:   and embedded power vs JSON SDUI.
130: - **Engagement**: reach out to adjacent open projects (LVGL for the embedded
131:   renderer, W3C WebUI) and present at FOSDEM/IETF/W3C-style venues; publish the
132:   validator as a reusable tool for any SDUI adopter.
133: 
134: ## 10. Timeline
135: 
136: | Milestone | Date |
137: |-----------|------|
138: | Submit proposal | Sept 3, 2026 (calls open) |
139: | Deadline | Nov 3, 2026, 12:00 CET |

144: ## 11. Deliverables & acceptance
145: 
146: All software FOSS (Apache-2.0); all open outcomes open access. Deliverables are
147: WCAG-compliant where they include web surfaces.
148: 
149: - [ ] `spec/README.md` + consolidated property registry (WP1)
150: - [ ] Schema + validator CLI + expanded conformance vectors, CI-gated (WP2)
151: - [ ] Fuzz harnesses (Rust/JS/Java) + C ABI Miri pass (WP3)
152: - [ ] Benchmark suite + comparison chart (WP4)
153: - [ ] **WCAG/ARIA compliance on the SSR HTML renderer** (WP5)
154: - [ ] CI green (rust + java), hosted demo URL, screenshots (WP5)
155: - [ ] NLnet final report + MoU deliverables (PM)
156: 
157: ## 12. Two-page narrative (copy-ready for the NLnet form)
158: 
159: **Proposal name:** Pathland — an implementable open UI-protocol standard.
160: 
161: **What it is.** Pathland is an open, Apache-2.0 protocol for declarative,
162: retained-mode UI that is language- and platform-agnostic. It describes *what* a
163: UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment — as a stream of fixed
164: **16-byte opcodes**, never *where*. Emission is diff-based and reactive: only the
165: nodes that changed emit, an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes, and renderers are
166: pure functions of the stream that map onto native elements (GTK4, DOM/HTML,
167: LVGL-planned). The engine is transport- and process-agnostic, running from
168: embedded dual-core to in-browser WASM to distributed server-driven backends.
169: The spec already exists (split across `spec/OPCODE`, `PRIMITIVES`, `MODIFIERS`,
170: `EVENTS`, `CONFORMANCE`, plus the `DSL` authoring surface) and is enforced by
171: golden byte vectors.
172: 
173: **What we will build.** This project turns the working proof-of-concept into an
174: **implementable open standard**: (1) a spec index and consolidated
175: property-key registry; (2) a machine-readable ID schema and cross-language
176: validator so the four language surfaces cannot drift; (3) coverage-guided fuzzing
177: and a Miri pass proving the decoders and the C ABI are robust against malformed
178: input; (4) a benchmark suite quantifying the 16-byte-vs-JSON/Protobuf claim; and
179: (5) CI, **WCAG/ARIA compliance on the HTML renderer**, and a hosted SSR HTML
180: demo as live evidence. A solo maintainer delivers
181: this in six months at 260 hours (cost-recovery, €11,700).
182: 
183: **Why it matters.** An open UI *protocol* — rather than another UI *framework* —
184: lets any EU vendor build renderers and DSLs against one spec, reducing lock-in to
185: US-owned stacks and supporting the Open Internet Stack's cross-platform
186: development goal. The 16-byte, zero-delta wire format is an efficiency answer to
187: bloated JSON SDUI. Prior art (Airbnb/Lyft/Spotify SDUI, Flutter, React Native)
188: is closed or runtime-coupled; nothing provides an open, diff-based binary
189: instruction stream across embedded, browser, desktop, and server.
190: 
191: **European dimension.** Made in Denmark; Apache-2.0; engagement with LVGL, W3C
192: WebUI, and EU open-source venues; the validator and conformance suite become a
193: reusable tool for any SDUI adopter.
